content:
Priya: Thanks everyone — quick follow-up from the runtime section of the all-hands. A few action items came up and I wanted to surface them here so engineers + leads can chime in.
Eli: +1. Can you list the top two perf concerns you heard?
Priya: Sure — 1) micro-batching thresholds causing unpredictable tail latency for short-chat workloads, 2) KV-cache TTLs and eviction policies making cache-hit curves noisy.
Jordan: For micro-batching: we currently batch up to 8 requests or 50ms whichever comes first. Observing lots of 45ms waits on 1–2 token requests.
Daria: Is 50ms the global default? We could make it adaptive based on qps and percentiles.
Eli: We already have per-model batch config but defaults are global. Proposal: introduce a per-route adaptive max-wait that uses 95th pct target latency. If qps low, reduce wait to 8–12ms.
Priya: That sounds good. How risky to roll out? Can we A/B for a subset of low-qps routes?
Jordan: Low-risk if gated behind canary flag. Implementation plan: metric: p95 latency pre/post, token/sec and cost-per-token. Rollout steps: dev -> canary(5%) -> canary(25%) -> global.
Daria: For KV cache: weird eviction spikes on long-tail prefixes. We should surface a TTL + size-based eviction and expose miss/reuse histograms.
Eli: Agreed. Also want to track stale KV entries causing regressed outputs for a small set of evals. Ops needs a way to flush per-deployment caches without full redeploy.
Priya: Noted. Is there a quick interim we can do?
Jordan: Add an admin endpoint to flush prefix cache and a CLI helper. Low-effort.
ops-bot: deploybot: Canary patch created for adaptive-batching (PR #4821) — awaiting approvals.
Daria: On kernels: leadership asked about gating new attention kernel rollout. We should define rollback criteria. My suggestion: rollback if p95 latency increases > 8% or model perplexity/regression on the customer eval set increases beyond a small delta.
Eli: Make that concrete: p95 > 6% for 10 minutes OR eval regression > 0.5% on key prompts. Also require automatic fallback to previous kernel if metrics trip.
Priya: Can we capture these rules as a JSON policy and store with the canary config? Ops/Platform can then enforce.
Jordan: Yep — I can add a schema. Also will add a dashboard: p50/p95/p99, error rate, KV-hit-rate, and eval-run baseline diff.
Daria: Who owns the eval baseline? Research or runtime?
Eli: Research owns the evals but runtime will run the smoke eval during canary. Need SLO on evaluation latency (shouldn't slow rollout).
Priya: Next steps: Jordan — prototype admin cache flush + canary schema by EOD Friday. Daria — draft rollback policy text and the eval prompt set. Eli — coordinate the canary enforcement and ops playbook. I'll sync with leadership after we have prototype.
Jordan: I’ll post a short PR with the schema and a small test harness.
ops-bot: alert: canary job scheduled for 2003123600 on staging cluster.
Eli: Thanks. One more ask from support: can we add a per-route flag to prefer lower-quantized kernels for lower cost for non-critical customers? Might interact with fallback logic.
Daria: That should be a routing policy param; we can add to the rollout matrix.
Priya: Great — keep updates here. If anyone wants to join the quick sync tomorrow 10am to triage the action items, reply here. :thumbsup:
